vulnerability.title: Stack-based buffer overflow in xmlSnprintfElements
vulnerability.upstreamDescription: In libxml2 before 2.15.4, xmlSnprintfElements in valid.c has a strcat stack-based buffer overflow.

componentPresence.codePresence: xmlSnprintfElements is present in the exact library. The Alpine debug package has the same GNU Build ID as the installed binary; DWARF maps the inlined routine/callsite and exact-library disassembly shows its strcat call sites.

prerequisites.cveRecordSpecificExploitPrerequisites: MITRE describes a stack-based strcat overflow in xmlSnprintfElements and gives CVSS local/low-complexity/no-privileges/no-user-interaction; it does not enumerate a complete exploit payload prerequisite.
prerequisites.codePathPrerequisitesFromSource: DTD validation reaches xmlValidateElementContent; a content-model mismatch with diagnostic formatting reaches xmlSnprintfElements at valid.c callsite line 5312. No exploit-specific input was generated or tested.
prerequisites.targetAssessment: PostgreSQL accepts SQL/XML input from authenticated database clients; the current database role is superuser and can install shipped extensions. Core parser calls omit XML_PARSE_DTDVALID, xmlvalidate is a not-implemented stub, and optional xml2 1.1 is not currently installed. Its shipped xml_valid(text) binds directly to xml_is_well_formed; its XPath/XSLT parse paths do not set XML_PARSE_DTDVALID. A disposable CREATE EXTENSION xml2 test returned true for the well-formed XML document that violates its internal DTD.

reachability.evidence: The vulnerable routine is called from the DTD-validation error-reporting path. PostgreSQL REL_17_11 parser options contain XML_PARSE_NOENT and XML_PARSE_DTDATTR (plus optional XML_PARSE_NOBLANKS), not XML_PARSE_DTDVALID. XPath/XMLTABLE parser calls use options 0. The xmlvalidate implementation raises FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED. A benign document that violated its internal DTD content declaration was accepted as well-formed and XMLPARSE returned it. Optional xml2 extension review: exact extension SQL and REL_17_11 sources show the same non-validating behavior, and a benign disposable test with CREATE EXTENSION xml2 returned true for a DTD-invalid but well-formed document. Benign disposable XML2 tests additionally passed the same DTD-inconsistent document through the shipped xpath_string and xslt_process functions.
reachability.applicationXmlReferences: No XML, XPath, XMLTABLE, XMLPARSE or XMLSERIALIZE references were found in apps/web, apps/worker or packages at pre-evidence analysis head.
reachability.qualification: XML parsing remains enabled and reachable; only the DTD validation operation required by this vulnerable reporting path is unavailable in the current PostgreSQL SQL implementation.
reachability.extensionAssessment: xml2 1.1 is available but not installed in the live database; only plpgsql is loaded. Current SQL role is superuser, so the extension was tested on a disposable exact-image database. Shipped xml_valid aliases xml_is_well_formed; XML2 XPath/XSLT parser paths omit XML_PARSE_DTDVALID; its module imports xmlReadMemory and has no direct imports of libxml2 validator functions. The exact-image disposable tests also ran xml2 xpath_string and xslt_process on DTD-inconsistent but well-formed input; both returned expected outputs.

attackerControl.assessment: The current database role is superuser=true and can issue arbitrary SQL, XML values, and install the shipped xml2 extension. Core PostgreSQL and the shipped xml2 extension still provide only well-formedness parsing/XPath/XSLT paths in this exact runtime; the xml2 xml_valid alias is xml_is_well_formed and no inspected path enables DTD validation. A custom extension/native code path is a material revalidation trigger.
attackerControl.targetInputControl: Authenticated current SQL role can control XML and can install xml2; its shipped validation-like function is only a well-formedness alias, and its parser code does not set XML_PARSE_DTDVALID, so inputs do not reach the vulnerable DTD-validation formatter through these current built-in/shipped paths.

networkPrivilegeContext.user: Steady-state PostgreSQL process UID/GID 70:70; image Config.User is empty and entrypoint establishes postgres user
networkPrivilegeContext.assessment: PostgreSQL is reachable by authenticated peers on the project-scoped Compose bridge; its port is not published on the host. User, capabilities and topology are recorded as context and are not the VEX justification.

mitigation.reachabilityConstraint: The core PostgreSQL XML SQL implementation and shipped xml2 1.1 extension do not expose DTD validation in the exact parser paths inspected. xml2 xml_valid is an alias to xml_is_well_formed; XPath/XSLT parser calls omit XML_PARSE_DTDVALID. This is a current API/call-path constraint, not a claim that the vulnerable component is absent or patched.
contextualControls: PostgreSQL port 5432 has no host publication; bridge network is project-scoped and Internal=false.

justification.rationale: The exact vulnerable code is present, linked and loaded, and PostgreSQL XML parsing is enabled. The vulnerable formatter is called on DTD-validation content-model diagnostic paths. Exact PostgreSQL 17.11 core source omits XML_PARSE_DTDVALID, uses options 0 for XPath/XMLTABLE reads, and leaves xmlvalidate unimplemented. The live database role is superuser and may install the shipped xml2 extension, so that path was also evaluated: current DB has only plpgsql installed; exact xml2 SQL binds xml_valid directly to xml_is_well_formed, its REL_17_11 XPath/XSLT code uses XML_PARSE_NOENT without XML_PARSE_DTDVALID, and a benign exact-image disposable test accepted a well-formed document violating its internal DTD through xml_valid. PostgreSQL 17 documentation says XML input is not validated against DTDs. This supports a proposal that the DTD-validation formatter is outside the current core and shipped-extension execution paths; it does not cover custom extensions/native code, and it is not self-approved. Benign disposable tests also passed that DTD-inconsistent but well-formed document through xml2 xpath_string and xslt_process.
